# Rule 4 - Don't Self-Antag
"Self-antagging" refers to causing any serious damage or harm to crew as a non-antagonist.
While you can be rude, hold grudges, and even be a nuisance to an extent, you shouldn't self-antag.
As a crew-aligned role, the majority of your shift should not be spent harassing, running from, or otherwise being a general nuisance to the [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] department as a whole. Nanotrasen would not hire someone that lacks basic understanding of law nor social expectations.
Free agents may act outside the realm of regular crew-sided roles; however, [bold]free agents should still prioritize their own life above all[/bold]. Ask in admin help (F1) before taking any action that may have significant impact on the round. Significance is defined by any action that may require extensive efforts to reverse or prevent by crew-sided roles.
## Precedents
- Don't start random fights without an in-character reason, also known as 'RDM' (Random Death Match). A drunken bar fight over an argument is fine; randomly attacking people in the halls because "your character is insane" is not. - [textlink="Don't over-escalate." link="RuleEscalate"] Someone calling you stinky is not a good enough reason for you to kill them. - Don't [bold]ever[/bold] round-remove people (meaning to prevent someone from being revived) as a non-antagonist. - Don't sabotage the station as a non-antagonist. Vandalizing the front of [color=#ba292c][bold]Security[/bold][/color] is fine — with proper escalation and in-character reasoning — but lube-bombing them out of the blue or smashing their windows is not. - Don't steal antagonist objectives or similar items of high importance as a non-antagonist. Hacking into a vending machine to steal some insulated gloves is fine; stealing the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Captain[/bold][/color]’s spare ID is not. - [color=#5ed7aa][bold]Silicons[/bold][/color] following their laws are not self-antagging, but they can be punished for excessive leaps of logic to perform self-antag-like actions. - [color=#a41683][bold]Clowns[/bold][/color] and [color=#776d66][bold]Mimes[/bold][/color] are partially exempt from the self-antag rules when in the pursuit of entertaining the crew. [bolditalic][color=#ffaa00]Only the self-antag rules.[/color][/bolditalic] This does not include departmental sabotage, nor anything that would cause significant or lasting damage. Should they abuse this clause, crew-aligned roles are allowed to beat the offending entertainer to crit with little escalation beforehand. Always ask in admin help (F1) if in doubt regarding this clause.
